cards.text: David has just taken down Goliath, and he's finished speaking with King Saul. That's when the souls of David and Jonathan, Saul's son (1 Samuel 14:1), are knit together. Jonathan loves David as himself.

cards.question: Before Goliath, David went back and forth between Saul and his father's sheep (1 Samuel 17:15). Now, from that day on, what does Saul do with David?

answers.text: Keeps him and won't let him go home
Sends him back to his father's sheep
Sends him home with great riches

cards.text: Then Jonathan makes a covenant with David, because he loves him as himself. Not “we should hang out sometime,” friend. A COVENANT.

cards.question: Jonathan takes off the robe he's wearing and gives it to David. What else does Jonathan give him?

cards.text: Saul sends David out again and again, then sets him over the men of war. From watching sheep to leading soldiers! Meanwhile I throw a party when a cookie comes out straight.

cards.question: Saul's officers are unhappy that David has been set over the men of war.

cards.text: As the troops head home after David killed the Philistine, the women come out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul. Singing, dancing, tambourines, the WHOLE parade!

cards.question: As the women dance, they sing a song about Saul and David. In their song, Saul gets credit for more than David.
The women sing that Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands. How does Saul take that song?

answers.text: He is furious and resents it
He joins right in and sings
He is proud of David for it

cards.text: “They have ascribed tens of thousands to David,” Saul says, “but only thousands to me. What more can he have but the kingdom?” The man got THOUSANDS, friend, and he's upset! I seal ONE cookie box and do a victory lap.

cards.question: After that song, from that day forward Saul kept a ___ eye on David.

cards.text: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God comes upon Saul, and he prophesies inside the house. David is playing the harp as usual, and Saul is holding a spear.

cards.question: Saul is holding a spear while David plays the harp. What does Saul do with it?

answers.text: He sets it down to listen

cards.question: Saul's spear pins David to the wall.
David slips away from the spear twice. Now Saul is afraid of David. Why?

answers.text: The LORD was with David and had left Saul
David had the whole army on his side
David had threatened to take the throne

cards.text: So Saul sends David away and gives him command of a thousand men. That's the king's way of saying, “Go work from the OTHER office.”

cards.question: Out there with his thousand men, David continued to ___ in all his ways, because the LORD was with him.

cards.text: Saul sees how successful David is, and he's afraid of him. The man is the KING, friend, and he's scared of the guy he sent to the other office.

cards.question: Saul fears David, but all Israel and Judah love him. Why do they love David?

answers.text: He leads them out to battle and back
He shares Goliath's plunder with them
He promises them a new king soon

cards.text: Then Saul makes David an offer: his older daughter Merab, in marriage. Just one condition: “Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles.”

cards.question: Saul's offer of Merab sounds generous. But what is Saul thinking on the inside?

answers.text: Let the Philistines take care of David
David will make a fine son-in-law
Merab will keep David loyal to him

cards.question: How does David answer Saul's offer of Merab?

answers.text: He asks who he is to become the king's son-in-law
He asks for land and riches to go along with her
He asks to fight the Philistines before the wedding

cards.question: When the time comes, Saul gives his daughter Merab to David in marriage.

cards.text: Nope. When it's time, Merab is given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah. It's like your boss says the promotion's yours, then hands it to somebody else at the meeting.
Now Saul's other daughter, Michal, loves David. When Saul hears about it, it pleases him.

cards.question: Why does the news that Michal loves David please Saul?

answers.text: He wants her to be a snare to David
He is glad to see his daughter happy
He hopes it will make Jonathan happy

cards.text: So Saul tells David, “For a second time now you can be my son-in-law.” A second time? Friend, the first time didn't even HAPPEN.

cards.question: Saul has his servants speak to David privately and tell him the king is pleased with him.
Saul's servants pass the message to David. What does David say about himself?

answers.text: He is a poor man and lightly esteemed
He is too busy fighting the king's battles
He is not ready to leave his father's house

cards.text: The servants report back, and Saul names his price: “The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.”

cards.question: That price isn't really about revenge. Saul intended to cause David's ___ at the hands of the Philistines.
When the servants tell David Saul's terms, David is pleased to become the king's son-in-law.

cards.text: Before the wedding day even arrives, David and his men head out against the Philistines.

cards.question: Saul asked for a hundred. How many Philistines do David and his men kill?

cards.text: David presents them as payment in full, and Saul gives him Michal in marriage. So the plan to get David killed... just made David his son-in-law.

cards.question: Saul realizes the LORD is with David and that Michal loves David. So Saul grows even more ___ of David.
From then on, Saul and David are at peace with each other.
Every time the Philistine commanders come out for battle, David is more successful than all of Saul's officers. So David's ___ was highly esteemed.

cards.text: Saul's got a jealous eye, and David's got the LORD. We'll stop the oven right here, friend, but this batch is NOT done baking.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 16 quotes "Go work from the OTHER office.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The setup says David 'slips away from the spear twice.' 1 Samuel 18:11 says Saul hurled it and 'David eluded him twice.' The text says David eluded Saul, not the spear, and it doesn't say how many times the spear was thrown. The card rewords what the text calls it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'David had the whole army on his side' can be argued true within the passage. 18:5 says David's command pleased all the people and Saul's officers, and 18:16 says all Israel and Judah loved David. A baker could defend this answer.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The question says 'Saul's offer of Merab sounds generous. But what is Saul thinking on the inside?' That framing rules out both wrong answers, which are friendly thoughts ('David will make a fine son-in-law', 'Merab will keep David loyal to him'). Only the hostile answer fits the 'But', so the setup gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'He is a poor man and lightly esteemed' uses Bible wording ('lightly esteemed'). The wrong answers are in modern everyday wording ('too busy fighting the king's battles', 'not ready to leave his father's house'). The right answer stands out because it sounds like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Samuel 18:26, but 'David and his men head out against the Philistines' comes from 18:27. The citation should be 1 Samuel 18:26-27.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 18:30 is already asked on card 19, so this last card should only say the story isn't over. Its first line, 'Saul's got a jealous eye, and David's got the LORD,' recaps earlier verses (18:9, 18:28) and moves nothing forward. The card also cites 18:30 but tells nothing from that verse.
